move: Measure chay days. First, ask the Global Diet Quality Project or Gallup to tabulate the 2021 flesh-free share (7.9% of adults ate no meat, poultry or fish on the previous day) by the lunar date of the recall day; then add a chay-day question to a probability survey (household living standards or nutrition survey)
who: Global Diet Quality Project and Gallup (tabulation); NSO; National Institute of Nutrition
indicative_cost: Very low for the tabulation; low (tens of thousands of USD) for a survey item
why_it_matters: Sizes Vietnam's largest plant-protein occasion and the cheapest displacement route; the 2021 data already cap chay person-days at about 8%
who_would_pay: No philanthropic payer found: Nova Vista excludes culture change, ACE Movement Grants now exclude diet change and ReRoot Asia excludes Vietnam. National survey budgets (NSO, NIN) or GAIN's Diet Quality Questionnaire, which already covers Vietnam

move: Analyse declaration-level customs data for HS 3504, 2106.10, 1109 and 2102.20.10 (yeast for animal feeding), 2024 to 2025, by importer and description
who: Researchers; MOF customs data; funders
why_it_matters: Splits food from feed, sizes the textured share of 2106.10 (the pool a T1 line serves) and names the buyers of imported plant protein and of feed yeast (T2)
who_would_pay: No full fit. Partial: Nova Vista (open data only as the evidence base for a procurement or market-commitment outcome); World Bank or ADB technical assistance. Otherwise industry (a would-be T1 or T2 owner)

move: Build Vietnamese sensory and choice-test capacity: blind tests of higher-protein chay and 20 to 30% blends; a price choice experiment
who: Universities (HUST, NIN, Can Tho); funders
why_it_matters: First tested evidence on acceptance and willingness to pay in Vietnam
who_would_pay: Bezos Centre for Sustainable Protein at NUS (consumer-acceptance platform covering East and Southeast Asia), with a Vietnamese institute. Partial: Coefficient Giving and GFI research grants (2026 rounds closed)

move: Run a randomised label and name test (chay, thuần chay, thực vật, giàu đạm; thịt nuôi cấy, thịt tế bào, thịt nhân tạo; lên men, vi sinh, biến đổi gen)
who: Researchers; funders
why_it_matters: Decides what to call new products before launch
who_would_pay: Bezos Centre for Sustainable Protein at NUS (fits). Partial: Nova Vista (naming as an input to a market-shaping outcome)

move: Canteen and school trial with one large caterer, as one move with three arms: (a) an extender or canteen protein ingredient in minced and processed-meat dishes (17% of canteen protein dishes); (b) a chay-day menu; (c) a school plant-slot and minced-dish arm, in which one caterer that writes one menu for several schools serves a textured-soy or blended dish in the plant slot and in one minced-meat or fish-cake dish, with daily published menus (Directive 33) as controls. Log the dish species replaced, protein per dish, served portions, plate waste and intake the next day
who: Contract caterers (for example Haseca, Hoang Kim, Hoa Sua); researchers; Humane World Viet Nam as implementer of the chay-day arm
why_it_matters: Tests the largest price-set channel and the lasting diet effect. Animals spared per meal differ about 34-fold between a pork and a chicken dish, and chicken leads only 13% of canteen protein dishes, so the result depends on the dish species logged
source_ids: CHN-41; GLB-39; UPL-27; UPL-32; PMR-02; PMR-24; FUF-01; FUF-03
who_would_pay: Arm (a): partly Nova Vista's procurement lever and the Bezos Centre's hybrid research. Arm (b): Humane World Viet Nam fits as implementer, but no current funder both covers Vietnam and funds diet change (Navigation Fund partial). Arm (c): no external payer found

move: In-store test of a protein-upgraded chay product in 20 minimarts, measuring price response and repeat
who: A chay maker; a chain; funders
why_it_matters: Revealed repeat purchase at a known price
who_would_pay: Industry: a chay maker and a chain (no external payer found)

move: Chay safety and composition survey: test borax, preservatives, microbes and protein first, and add animal DNA as a low-cost PCR screen (QUATEST 3 tests 86 species at 0.001%); publish with VFA, publish methods and do not name small makers
who: Can Tho University; QUATEST 3; Vietnam Food Administration
why_it_matters: Chay's live trust problems are borax, microbes and unlabelled origin (no confirmed case of meat in chay from 2015 to 2026); gives makers protein targets; the 2016 fish-sauce survey, which named makers, led to delistings and a backlash against the testers
who_would_pay: No full fit. Partial: Bezos Centre at NUS, UNICEF Viet Nam, ACIAR; food-safety authorities' own budgets

move: Standing panel of 10 to 15 research and procurement buyers (specifications, minimum orders, qualification times)
who: An industry association; AltProtein Vietnam
why_it_matters: Answers the most important unknown for a founder: how long qualification takes
who_would_pay: No full fit. Partial: Nova Vista, Coefficient Giving. Otherwise industry (an industry association)

move: Estimate the share of meat eaten as processed products (giò, chả, sausages, canned, fillings)
who: Meat processors' association; NSO
why_it_matters: The second most influential assumption in the demand model
who_would_pay: Industry: meat processors' association; NSO's own budget (no external payer found)

move: Hotel and menu audit in Nha Trang (20 food-and-beverage managers, 30 menus)
who: AltProtein Vietnam
why_it_matters: Tests the tourism hypothesis cheaply
who_would_pay: Humane World Viet Nam fits as implementer, not funder. Partial: Nova Vista, Navigation Fund. Otherwise AltProtein Vietnam's own budget

move: Request quotes for one vegetable and one plant-protein wrapped SKU from three EU importers of Asian frozen foods and two brand owners already sourcing wrapped foods from Vietnam, with their certification (IFS or BRCGS) and origin requirements; retailer protein targets need no survey, since they are published
who: Trade promotion bodies; exporters of wrapped foods
why_it_matters: Tests export demand through the buyers who already take Vietnamese wrapped foods (stuffed pasta exports USD 128.2 million in 2023) where Vietnam has a tariff edge
who_would_pay: Industry and trade bodies (no external payer found)

move: Feed carbon-footprint benchmark for Vietnamese shrimp and pangasius feed
who: Feed mills; ASC; researchers
why_it_matters: Helps ASC-certified mills meet GHG reporting (ASC Feed Standard 1.21.4 and 1.21.5); will not by itself create demand for microbial ingredients
who_would_pay: No full fit. Partial: ADB Ventures, IFC, ACIAR, World Bank or ADB technical assistance. Otherwise industry (ASC-certified mills)

move: Ask MOH or VFA to state that an unqualified chay or thuần chay claim means the vegan criteria of TCVN 13625:2023, that egg or milk must be named in a qualifier, and that allium-free stays voluntary; enforce the existing goods-label rules against false chay claims, paired with DMV-07 testing
who: MOH; Vietnam Food Administration
why_it_matters: TCVN 13625:2023 already defines vegetarian and vegan claims but counts egg, milk and honey as vegetarian and says nothing on alliums; false chay claims are already unlawful, so the need is guidance and enforcement, not a new rule
who_would_pay: No full fit. Partial: Nova Vista (policy outcome); ACE Movement Grants for a small Vietnamese organisation (policy work only)

move: A voluntary industry code for generic product names (giò lụa, xúc xích, hotdog) that states the meat share when a plant or fungal protein replaces 10% or more of the meat. Percentage labelling of a named meat is already law (Decree 37/2026, carrying Decree 43/2017 Art 13(4))
who: Meat processors (Vissan, Masan MEATLife, C.P. Vietnam); a processors' association; MOIT
why_it_matters: Defensive: proof against a độn (filler) accusation. Declared percentages are already enforced criminally, and the fraud frame lives in unlabelled market giò and exempt small businesses, which a label rule does not reach
who_would_pay: Industry (processors); for the policy side only partial fits (Nova Vista, ACE Movement Grants)

move: Defend the permissive naming regime in the new Food Safety Law decree (no rule reserves thịt, sữa or phô mai; names must only not mislead, and practice already qualifies meat words, as in Heo hầm chay) and aim vocabulary guidance at state and media use, which has used thịt nhân tạo for cultivated meat
who: MOH; Vietnam Food Administration; provincial science departments
why_it_matters: Keeps qualified meat and milk words usable and removes a naming penalty before the first new products arrive
who_would_pay: Nova Vista (fits: fair naming and novel-food pathways); ACE Movement Grants for a small Vietnamese organisation (policy work only, USD 100,000 or less, deadline 18 October 2026)

move: Ask MAE and VFA whether a recombinant protein identical to the native protein is a detectable product of the modified gene under Joint Circular 45/2015 Art 1(2)(a), and whether a product containing one below 5% of ingredients may still claim non-GMO
who: MAE and MOH (joint note; policy option in chapter 27)
why_it_matters: The GMO label applies only above 5% of ingredients, so lactoferrin-type uses (about 0.08%) are not caught; what remains open is high-inclusion uses and the voluntary non-GMO claims the likely Vietnamese buyers make
who_would_pay: Nova Vista (fits: novel-food pathways); ACE Movement Grants for a small Vietnamese organisation (policy work only, deadline 18 October 2026)

move: National school guidance (Decision 3958/QĐ-BYT) already has no animal share. Ask MOET, NIN and Ajinomoto to replace the menu software's 'animal protein at least 48%' default with protein-quality, zinc and iron targets per lunch (by absorption band) and a sodium limit, and to add textured soy and legume products, with phytate data, to the software food list; write both into the MOET bán trú circular due in 2026 and the digital menu tools due in 2027 to 2028 (Decision 973/QĐ-TTg). A second version: a procurement standard for innovative protein in public and state-enterprise canteens
who: MOET; MOH and NIN; Ajinomoto Vietnam (menu software); provinces
why_it_matters: The software default, not national guidance, prints the animal floor on school menus; guidance already asks for animal protein on 4 to 5 days a week and plant protein at least twice; supplier documents are now set by Directive 33/CT-TTg. The gain is protein quality, zinc and cost per gram, not meat displacement, since the plant slot is filled with tofu
who_would_pay: No full fit. As protein quality in school food it fits UNICEF Viet Nam's 2027 to 2031 programme (school food standards); as a canteen procurement standard it fits Nova Vista's procurement lever. Other partial fits: Bezos Centre, Humane World, World Bank or ADB

move: Create national eight-digit customs subheadings for soy isolate, pea protein and textured protein
who: MOF
why_it_matters: Makes business-to-business demand visible every year
who_would_pay: No full fit. Partial: Nova Vista; World Bank or ADB technical assistance. Otherwise MOF's own budget

move: Publish an origin note for wrapped-food exporters on the EU 20% cap on non-originating flour, starch and rice and on the 10% tolerance for imported textured soy in 2106 foods (by weight or value), and on claiming CPTPP for the UK; imported soy protein is not the main constraint. Keep the EU, UK, Japanese and Canadian preferences usable
who: MOIT (origin office); VCCI; exporters
why_it_matters: Keeps a 6 to 17.4 point export edge usable (Japan charges 3.9% on Vietnamese dumplings under CPTPP against 21.3% for China and Thailand)
who_would_pay: Industry and trade bodies (no external payer found; World Bank or ADB technical assistance partial)

move: Obtain a written Ministry of Finance ruling on whether soy milk (TCVN 12443:2018), nut and cereal milks above 5 g total sugar per 100 ml are nước giải khát (soft drinks) under the sugary-drink excise, before 1 January 2027
who: MOF (tax department); plant-milk makers (Vinasoy, Vinamilk, TH, Nutifood) and their association
why_it_matters: The excise is 8% from 2027 and 10% from 2028 above 5 g sugar per 100 ml, and dairy is exempt; core Fami soy milks carry 6.5 to 9.3 g; plant-milk design and the host drink for T10 depend on the answer
who_would_pay: Industry (plant-milk makers and their association); no external payer found

move: Publish a price sheet of five delivered quotes for food-grade, low-temperature defatted soy flour and three for Chinese plain textured soy, with the T1 breakeven (flour below about USD 700 to 940 per t for a 1 t/h line at 70% utilisation)
who: A would-be T1 owner (chay maker, co-packer or distributor); AltProtein Vietnam
why_it_matters: Delivered flour is 63 to 85% of the cost of domestic textured soy and sets the sign of the T1 margin; the sheet decides the T1 kill test
who_would_pay: Industry (the would-be owner or its lender); no external payer needed
